title: When the Spire Sings
premise: Beatrix Dunmore, a runaway apprentice who keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that every entry he has ever recorded is a thread holding his country together. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, the nation begins to be unwritten, and Beatrix learns the guild's founder traded its existence to buy a thirteenth moon-turn of borrowed time. Guided by the spire that sings in ledger-script and the found family of misfit guildsmen who refuse to abandon him, Beatrix must locate the one true door out of a country that is forgetting itself. In the end he chooses to rewrite the founding bargain at the cost of his own memories of home, saving everyone but losing his belonging — until his found family teaches him that memory can be rebuilt from love rather than ledgers.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed heirlooms before turning to fantasy. They write about people who keep records of things the world would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He catalogs an impossible thing — a key that opens yesterday — while hiding from the hedge-witch who trained him. Establishes the guild, his loneliness, and his gift for seeing the threads binding objects to stories. Emotional beat: quiet yearning for a place to belong.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons on the Wall
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Oren Vey's POV. The guild's oldest mural shows twelve moons; a thirteenth has appeared overnight. Oren conceals the omen from the guild while interrogating the key Beatrix logged. Emotional beat: dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Sent to repair a border ward-stone, he meets Sable, a ward-breaker turned reluctant ally, who warns the wards don't keep enemies out — they hold the country's story in place. Emotional beat: first crack in everything Beatrix believes.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The wards fall and every star vanishes in one breath; the horizon simply ends where the country used to continue. Beatrix saves a child from a street that forgets itself mid-step. Emotional beat: terror and the instinct to protect strangers.

chapters.title: A Guild of Misfits
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Survivors shelter in the guildhall: Oren, Sable, the cartographer Ilex who maps places that no longer exist, and cook-mage Bramble. Beatrix realizes the guild's impossible trades were maintenance work on reality. Emotional beat: belonging offered, distrusted.

chapters.title: Entries in a Dead Hand
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He finds the founder's hidden ledger: the country was traded away, one memory per page, to buy thirteen turns of the moon. His own apprenticeship entry is signed in the founder's hand. Emotional beat: betrayal and terrible purpose.

chapters.title: The Spire Begins to Sing
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. The central spire emits a tone only readable as ledger-script, listing what has already been erased. Villages are gone; so are their names from every mouth. Emotional beat: grief for the forgotten.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Moon
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. Oren confesses he helped the founder make the trade and has been paying installments with his own past. He gives Beatrix the founder's compass, which points not north but toward doors. Emotional beat: guilt passed like an inheritance.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Sable travel toward the capital through land being unwritten; roads loop, rivers run backward, and travelers they meet have no faces yet. Sable reveals she once broke a ward for money and regrets it. Emotional beat: trust forged on the road.

chapters.title: The Archive of Unmade Things
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. In the capital's drowned archive, the party finds the original contract — and learns the door out exists but opens only for someone who belongs nowhere. Beatrix fits the description too well. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into fear.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He discovers gaps in his own memory: his mother's face, his reason for running from the hedge-witch. The erasure has been eating him since chapter one. Emotional beat: identity unraveling.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch Returns
chapters.summary: Maren the hedge-witch arrives, having walked out of the unwritten lands alive. She reveals Beatrix ran away because she tried to sell his thread-sight to the founder's agents. Emotional beat: rage, then complicated forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: Turn Twelve Begins
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. With one turn left, the guild splits: some want to flee through the door, others to fight. Oren's memories fail publicly; he forgets Beatrix's name mid-sentence. Emotional beat: a mentor becoming a stranger.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Last Map
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Ilex draws a map of the whole country from memory as an act of defiance, giving it weight enough to slow the erasure. It costs her her ability to picture anything new. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Doors in the Dark
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Sable follow the compass to a field of standing doors, each locked to a different life Beatrix might have lived. The founder's voice speaks through them, offering escape if he abandons the country entirely. Emotional beat: temptation made architectural.

chapters.title: The Founder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in the founder's POV, centuries earlier: a dying nation, a desperate trade, and the belief that someone with thread-sight could someday unpick it. Emotional beat: sympathy for the villain's grief.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Back at the guildhall, the misfits stage a festival of remembered things — songs, recipes, names — feeding the spire enough story to sing louder than the erasure. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The final moon rises; the spire's song becomes a scream. Beatrix enters the spire's heart where the contract is written into the stone, with Maren, Sable, and the fading Oren holding the door. Emotional beat: resolve against annihilation.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Founding Line
chapters.summary: Climax. Beatrix uses his thread-sight to amend the contract: not escape, but exchange — his own memories of home as payment to restore the country's. The stars return one by one as he forgets why he is crying. Emotional beat: sacrifice at the cost of self.

chapters.title: A Country That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Dawn restores the borders; the returned nation doesn't know what it owes. Sable keeps vigil over Beatrix, who wakes a stranger to himself. Emotional beat: tenderness toward the emptied.

chapters.title: Ledgers Written in Other Hands
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The guild shows him the evidence of who he was — entries, the festival's songs, Maren's awkward apology — letting him choose his history rather than inherit it. He signs the guild ledger anew. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt by choice.

chapters.title: When the Spire Sings
chapters.summary: Final chapter, shared POV. A year later, the spire sings softly each dusk, and the guild trades in small impossibilities again. Beatrix keeps the ledgers, keeps the people, and writes a new entry: a key that opens tomorrow. Emotional beat: home as something made, not found.
